method: Five seconds of real CDP wheel events (Input.dispatchMouseEvent, one every 16 ms, not waiting for each acknowledgement; about 300 are sent) on the 200-component canvas at 30% zoom, the selected component in the middle of the stage (about a dozen components on screen, the selection overlay and handles drawn), while a Chromium trace (Tracing domain: devtools.timeline, frame, cc, viz) records. Frame duration = the time between the presentations of consecutive frames that wanted an update (compositor PipelineReporter events inside the window): 16.7 ms when every vsync made a frame, 33.3 ms after a missed one. Missed vsyncs by draw interval, dropped frames (compositor label), long tasks (RunTask on CrRendererMain over 16.7 ms) and rAF intervals are reported alongside. Four runs: "pan" scrolls 12 px per event back and forth about 300 px around the selection; "panWithZoom" is the same with every twelfth event a Ctrl-wheel zoom step (one notch, 1.27x; in for a second, out for a second); "sweepWithZoom" scrolls 25 px per event the same way for the whole run (about 7,500 px, the selected component leaves the screen), so new components are un-culled and rasterised throughout, with zoom steps. A fourth run, "overview", is the sweep with zoom steps starting at 6% (the minimum is 5%), where about fourteen components are on screen. Reported raw and rounded to whole vsyncs (see above). Pass, in the three 30% runs: whole-vsync p95 <= 16.7 ms and at most 2% of frames that missed a vsync (>= 25 ms) or were dropped; the overview run (about 55 components un-culled and painted, 9 ms of layerisation on every frame that paints) is the weak spot and is held to 3%. Pixels are rasterised on the CPU (--disable-gpu). The benchmark never gives the page a transform.
